record.paper_title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
record.original_question: Extend the Section 5 transformation results to other discretization families: first to hybridized versions of augmented mixed methods in which an auxiliary variable g_h is introduced and the approximate flux q_h is defined from q_h = a g_h when c = a^{-1} is hard to compute; and then, if possible, to the continuous Galerkin method, potentially via the Staggered DG method or via Voralík's orthogonal-projection result for locally postprocessed mixed methods.

evidence.quote: Other methods. When the matrix c:=a^{-1} is not easy to compute, one can define the auxiliary variable g_h∈V_h ... to define the approximate flux q_h∈V_h ... Extending the results of Sect. 5 to the hybridized form of these sometimes called augmented mixed methods should be immediate; see the analysis in the 2018 paper [ 57 ].

The extension of these results to the continuous Galerkin method is an interesting possibility. Maybe the extension to the Staggered DG method [ 13 ] would provide a way to proceed in that case, because this method displays partial continuity of the scalar unkown and because it has been proved to be a limiting case of HDG methods; see [ 14 , 15 ]. Another possibility is to use a result by Voralík [ 100 , Theorem 7.1] which establishes that the solution of the continuous Galerkin method is an orthogonal projection of the locally postprocessed mixed method.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order elliptic boundary value problem
   -∇·(a ∇u) = f  in Ω ⊂ ℝ^d,    u = 0 on ∂Ω,
where Ω is a bounded polyhedral domain and a is a symmetric positive-definite coefficient matrix. Introducing the flux q = -a∇u, the mixed form reads
   c q + ∇u = 0,   ∇·q = f,
with c := a^{-1}. On a conforming simplicial mesh T_h with faces F_h, suppose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) discretization yields approximations (q_h, u_h, û_h) ∈ V_h × W_h × M_h that, after element-by-element local solvers and a hybridization argument, can be transformed into an equivalent formulation whose only globally coupled unknown is the numerical trace û_h ∈ M_h, satisfying a symmetric positive-definite system; assume moreover that this transformation provides energy-norm and superconvergence error estimates for the scalar variable and for a local postprocessing.

(1) Suppose that the matrix c = a^{-1} is difficult to evaluate, so that an "augmented mixed" approach is used: introduce an auxiliary variable g_h ∈ V_h satisfying a discrete relation enforcing g_h ≈ ∇u, and define the approximate flux by q_h = a g_h, with corresponding hybridized formulation. Establish the analogue of the above hybridization/transformation results (well-posedness via a global trace system, equivalence with the original mixed system, and the corresponding a priori error and superconvergence estimates) for these hybridized augmented mixed methods.

(2) Extend the same transformation framework to the standard continuous Galerkin (CG) finite element approximation of the elliptic problem, possibly by passing through the Staggered Discontinuous Galerkin (SDG) method—which exhibits partial continuity of the scalar unknown and arises as a limiting case of certain HDG methods—or by exploiting the orthogonal-projection identification of the CG solution with a locally postprocessed mixed-method solution.

Prove or disprove that such extensions hold, and identify the precise classes of stabilization and local-solver choices for which they do.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this extension problem could be located. The question is posed as an open direction for hybridization-based transformation results, and search did not surface a paper claiming to extend such HDG transformation results to hybridized augmented mixed methods or to the continuous Galerkin method via SDG/Vohralík's projection identity.

status_evidence.title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including extensions to hybridized augmented mixed methods and to the continuous Galerkin method via Staggered DG or Vohralík's orthogonal-projection result.
status_evidence.claim: The extension is explicitly listed as an open problem.
